lens: Master plan fit — does flattening specs/ topology advance or distort the master plan?
artifacts_reviewed: origin/dev:specs/ tree listing (30+ files at flat root)
fit_rationale: PR #18 is the explicit specs/ parallel of ADR-0115's registry consolidation: flat singular root, semantic basenames as direct children, retired the redundant `cross-cutting/` scope segment which the v4 BNF already declares as the omitted-default scope token. ADR-0119 is added in the same PR (docs/decisions/ADR-0119-specs-flat-root-topology.md, +116 lines, status=Accepted, deciders=council-architecture+council-foundry-vcs) and explicitly cites ADR-0115 as the precedent pattern — exactly the durable-decision shape that PR #15 was faulted for omitting. Per [[feedback_milestone_phase_hierarchy]] the 3-level Milestone>Phase>IP hierarchy lives under .omc/plans/milestones/ and is path-orthogonal to specs/ root topology, so flattening does NOT collapse scope; the IP frontmatter only updates string refs (e.g. `specs/lifecycle-configs/*.json`) keeping the lifecycle-configs family directory intact as a typed grouping (the one justified non-flat retention). Per [[feedback_flat_product_catalog]] + [[feedback_glossary_shared_not_platform]] the everything-is-shared / flat-catalog principle directly endorses removing the `cross-cutting/` scope token since shared IS the default. Per [[feedback_no_silent_regression]] this is the OPPOSITE of silent regression: ADR-0119 + ADR-0115 citation + git mv (history preserved) + comprehensive ref rewrite across 222 files including 8 ADRs, all 20 standards, 6 handoffs, project-memory.json, and all M-CC-P11/M02 IP frontmatters. Verified on origin/dev: zero `specs/cross-cutting/` strings remain in crates/, docs/, .omc/; zero files remain under that prefix in the tree.
antithesis_steelman: PR #18 is a topology change masquerading as a cleanup: (a) flattening removes a meaningful affordance — `cross-cutting/` told readers 'this spec is scope-neutral / cross-product'; under flat-root a reader can no longer distinguish a cross-cutting spec from a future product-scoped spec by inspection, only by reading the spec body; (b) ADR-0119 is authored AND merged in the same PR that executes the move (one-shot self-ratification), the same anti-pattern PR #15 was dinged for under the ADR-0019 protocol-mutation rule; (c) the lifecycle-configs family is retained as a typed sub-directory, which is the correct shape — but if grouping IS justified for lifecycle configs, the same argument could justify a `cross-cutting/` grouping for the cross-cutting family; the decision to flatten one and group the other rests on the assertion that cross-cutting IS the default, which is true today but constrains future product-scoped spec additions (they would have to introduce `specs/<product>/` siblings, making `specs/<basename>.json` implicitly mean cross-cutting forever); (d) 222 files of mechanical rewrite ossifies the new path as hard-coded string references in 14 Rust crates rather than a single registry-owned topology constant, repeating the abstraction miss A4 flagged on PR #15; (e) the doctrinal-substrate paths (decision-principles, forbidden-operations, oyatie-doctrine, masterplan, master-plan-sequencing, multispectrum-review) are the highest-blast-radius citation targets in the repo — moving them in one PR makes every prior evidence file that quoted the old path drift overnight unless the PR rewrites evidence too (it does for live citations, but historical audit-chain rows that literally quoted the old string now read as fiction).
tradeoff_tension: Doctrinal-path stability vs topology cleanliness. Doctrinal substrate paths (decision-principles, forbidden-operations, oyatie-doctrine, masterplan) are cited by ADRs, handoffs, plans, and audit-chain rows as their authority anchor; rewriting them at scale (even with `git mv` preserving log history) creates a permanent before/after seam in any text search across the repo's history and any external tool that snapshotted the old paths. Cleanliness reward is a one-token-shorter path and ADR-0115 parity. Tension cannot be ignored because the substrate is precisely the surface that doctrine [[feedback_no_silent_regression]] flags as needing version bumps + sunset notes for breaking changes — and the PR does ADR + ref-rewrite but does NOT add a `_migrated_from` back-pointer in any of the moved spec files (verified: ADR-0119's repository_layout section lists new paths but the moved JSONs themselves carry no migration breadcrumb in their top-level metadata). The grouped-vs-flat decision for lifecycle-configs vs everything-else is also asymmetric: justified, but the justification (typed family consumed together) could apply to other future families and the PR does not state the test for when a sub-directory IS justified.
synthesis: Strong accept as plan-advancing. Synthesis improvements (non-blocking, follow-on): (1) add a `_migrated_from: specs/cross-cutting/<basename>.json` breadcrumb in the top-level metadata of each moved spec for one milestone, then drop in the next, so external tools and historical citation chains get a single grace cycle; (2) extend ADR-0119 (or a one-line addendum) with the explicit test for when a sub-directory IS justified vs flat (the lifecycle-configs precedent: 'a typed family consumed by a single lane'), so future spec additions have a deterministic rule rather than relying on case-by-case judgement; (3) optionally introduce a registry-owned topology constant referenced by the 14 Rust crates that hard-code `specs/<basename>.json` (same A4 abstraction concern PR #15 raised, applies here at equal scale).

principle_violations.evidence: PR authors and self-ratifies ADR-0119 in the same change that executes the topology move it governs. ADR-0019 contemplates a separate update cycle for protocol-class ADRs. Mitigated by: ADR-0119 is a NEW ADR (not a mutation of an existing protocol ADR), and ADR-0115 is the established precedent it cites — so the protocol-mutation concern that bit PR #15 (which patched ADR-0019 line 105 in the same PR that changed the thing ADR-0019 governs) does NOT apply here at the same severity. Still LOW because authoring + executing in one PR limits review independence.

Doctrinal-substrate spec paths (oyatie-doctrine, masterplan, master-plan-sequencing, decision-principles, forbidden-operations, multispectrum-review) are public citation surfaces. PR rewrites every live citation in-tree (verified: 0 hits for `specs/cross-cutting/` on origin/dev across crates/, docs/, .omc/) and adds ADR-0119 + version-bump-equivalent (new ADR ratifying the topology). NOT silent. Severity LOW only because moved JSONs themselves carry no `_migrated_from` breadcrumb in metadata — external snapshots / cached agent contexts cannot self-resolve the move without consulting ADR-0119.

14 Rust crates patched to update hard-coded `specs/cross-cutting/<basename>.json` strings to `specs/<basename>.json`. Both old and new are hard-coded path strings in CLI/check layer; PR does not introduce a registry-owned topology constant. Not net-worse than the pre-PR state (which had the same hard-coding under a longer path), but the centralization opportunity is missed — identical to the A4 concern PR #15 raised.

ADR-0119 ships full sections (Context / Decision / Naming-justification table / Migration / Consequences / Rejected-alternatives / Verification / References). DOC-CATALOG.md is updated in the PR (+3/-3). doc-coverage doctrine SATISFIED — flagged only to record the contrast with PR #15 which omitted the DOC-CATALOG row.

findings: PR #18 IS the specs/ parallel of ADR-0115 (registries flat consolidation) — explicitly cited in ADR-0119 Context section first paragraph: 'ADR-0115 established the current topology cleanup pattern: use a flat canonical root, keep the semantic basename, and remove redundant cross-cutting scope directories.' The parallel is intentional and named, not coincidental.

Specs flat-root migration is COMPLETE on origin/dev: tree listing shows 30+ flat children at specs/ root plus the retained typed family specs/lifecycle-configs/; ZERO files remain under specs/cross-cutting/; ZERO `specs/cross-cutting/` string hits across crates/, docs/, .omc/.
ADR-0119 (+116 lines) added in the same PR provides the durable decision the prior pr-15-M2-r1 review found missing on PR #15 — this PR does NOT repeat that anti-pattern.

[[feedback_milestone_phase_hierarchy]] is NOT undermined: 3-level milestone>phase>IP hierarchy lives under .omc/plans/milestones/M-CC-cross-cutting/phases/P<NN>-<concern>/IP-<NNN>-<slug>.md; the IP frontmatters in this PR only rewrite the `specs/cross-cutting/<x>.json` string in their `source_spec` / `agent_prerequisites` / `decision_log` fields. Hierarchy depth at the plan tree is unchanged; only the spec path string each IP cites is shortened.

[[feedback_flat_product_catalog]] + [[feedback_glossary_shared_not_platform]] are AFFIRMED: removing the `cross-cutting/` scope token operationalizes the everything-is-shared principle (cross-cutting IS the default scope, so the token was redundant). ADR-0119 Naming-justification table repeats this rationale per row: 'cross-cutting is the omitted default scope.'

Lifecycle-configs family retention (specs/lifecycle-configs/) is the one justified non-flat retention; ADR-0119 explicitly distinguishes 'typed family consumed together by lifecycle fitness lanes' as the test — this is the correct shape but the test itself is buried in the per-row table rather than stated as the general rule for future families.
PR replaces #14 explicitly to remove unsigned commit f2c0696 — verification posture (signed replacement on the same tree) is doctrine-aligned with the Foundry pipeline admission gate.

Verification recorded in PR body: `git diff --cached --check`, `jq empty on changed JSON/JSONL`, `cargo run -q -p oya-foundry-vcs-admission-gate-app`, `cargo check --workspace --locked`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --locked: 2725 passed`. All four are direct cargo / git invocations consistent with the 2026-05-16 deprecation of external coordination tooling.

Multiple stale-ref concerns observed in working tree (26 grep hits for `specs/cross-cutting` in current branch) are NOT introduced by PR #18 — they are pre-PR-merge state in the current working branch (oya-m01-m02-gate-usecase-doc-drift); origin/dev (the PR merge target/base) shows zero hits. The concerns surface as PRE-EXISTING work-in-progress drift on the current branch, not regression introduced by PR #18.
uncertainty_areas: Whether external snapshots (agent caches, evidence audit-chain rows that literally quoted the old path) have been audited for the path move beyond the in-tree rewrite — ADR-0119 Migration section does not enumerate out-of-tree consumers.

Whether a same-cycle follow-up PR introduces the registry-owned topology constant to retire the 14 Rust crates' hard-coded `specs/<basename>.json` strings — if not, the abstraction debt is now durable.

Whether the test for 'when a sub-directory IS justified vs flat' (lifecycle-configs precedent) is documented as a general rule anywhere outside ADR-0119's per-row table — needed for future spec additions to be deterministic.
